subject: general
question: Rakesh’s salary is ₹12,000 per month. He spends ₹6,000 on house rent, ₹3,000 on bills and the rest of the amount is his monthly savings. Find his savings (in ₹) in a year, if in the month of his birthday, he spent his complete monthly savings for the birthday celebration
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Monthly Savings** = 12,000 − (6,000 + 3,000) = ₹3,000.

Savings are done for 11 months only (as 1 month savings spent on birthday).

**Yearly Savings** = 3,000 × 11 = ₹33,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹33,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Monthly Salary = ₹12,000 | **Rent** = ₹6,000 | **Bills** = ₹3,000.

**Formula:** Savings = Income − Expenditure

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c1a9d8237eabf1a6ae919f1bf75aea2b2caab57482c4de22d871df9a0daffd0c.png] 

⇒ **Monthly Expenditure** = ₹6,000 + ₹3,000 = ₹9,000

⇒ **Monthly Savings** = ₹12,000 − ₹9,000 = ₹3,000

⇒ Since **birthday month** savings are spent, savings occur for **11 months**.

⇒ **Annual Savings** = 11 × 3,000 = ₹33,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹33,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Monthly vs Annual Calculation

Always identify the number of effective periods. Annual Value = Monthly Value × 12, but adjust for specific non-saving months.

Percentage Savings

Savings Percentage = (Savings ÷ Income) × 100. In this case, (3,000 ÷ 12,000) × 100 = 25%.
